Messages.Author: John Flournoy
Messages.Body:
cowf...@hotmail.com (cowfields) wrote in message news:<1a6c91db.03100...@posting.google.com>...



That is exactly how it works, yes. And it's not particularly
overpowered, given the numbers of ways to stop it (block the action to
put BoC on the minion, play Seduction so he can't attempt to block,
rush that vamp into torpor, etc). Besides which, you could argue that
Awe or Voter Captivations are equally overpowered - at every
tournament I've ever seen, there's at least two decks using Voter
Cap/Awe; at one Lambach-storyline tournament 6 of 10 decks were
Presence vote. I've never, ever seen Blessing of Chaos at a table,
even in casual play. (Though I suspect I will be seeing more of it
soon.)

Yes, Blessing of Chaos can hurt Presence vote decks or Dominate
bleed-modifier decks. That's part of the game; just about every
powerful strategy has a simple counter. (Rush? Secure Haven! Intercept
wall? Daring the Dawn! Combat ends? Immortal Grapple! Immortal
Grapple? High Ground on a flight minion! and so on.) The trick is
figuring out what defenses to use in your limited-card-slot decks.

-John Flournoy
